title: The Bear and the Fox
summary: A large brown bear loved to boast of his extraordinary gentleness, piety, and benevolence to all the woodland creatures. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that hypocrisy that pretends to spare the dead while preying upon the living deserves no praise.
full_text: A large brown bear loved to boast of his extraordinary gentleness, piety, and benevolence to all the woodland creatures. Standing before a gathering of animals, he puffed out his broad chest and declared: "I am the most compassionate beast in all creation! Look at the lions, tigers, and wolves—how savagely they tear into living flesh! But as for me, I have such tender reverence for mortal life that I have never in all my years touched, harmed, or eaten a human corpse; I leave the departed to rest in peace!" The other beasts nodded in polite admiration of his noble virtue. But the clever fox stepped forward, tilted his head, and remarked with a biting smile: "Your piety would be far more convincing, Master Bear, if you showed the same tender mercy to the living that you show to the dead! You may spare the corpses who can feel no pain, but you slaughter the living with your claws without a single tremor of regret!"
moral: Hypocrisy that pretends to spare the dead while preying upon the living deserves no praise.

quiz.question: What essential truth does "The Bear and the Fox" teach young readers?
options: Hypocrisy that pretends to spare the dead while preying upon the living deserves no praise.
Might and physical strength always triumph over truth and wisdom
Flattery is the safest and most honest way to make lifelong friends
It is wise to pretend to be someone you are not in times of trouble

discussion_questions.prompt: Who are the central characters in "The Bear and the Fox", and what was each trying to accomplish at the beginning?

Were the consequences faced by the characters fair? What alternative choice could have produced a wiser outcome?
Imagine if the characters met again one year later. How would their behavior change based on what they learned today?
